answer: Climbing forty poles and checking every insulator costs a forger 11,300 in wages and bribes, and the forgery still fails at the first mile post. The lineman climbs each pole in turn, tests the insulators and writes the state of the line in the mile log. A karst mile claimed as inspected fails the log: the insulators must have been touched at the pigment of the pole, and a pole never climbed still wears its cracked glass, while the velvet entry in the log is read at every storm, so a mile whose poles were never climbed is left dead.
